page.h1: A Klue alternative for teams without a CI budget
page.subtitle: Klue is a full competitive intelligence platform for enablement teams. If you mainly need to know what your competitors changed each week, WebMonitor does that from $29 a month with no contract.
page.intro: Klue is built for companies with a competitive intelligence program: someone who curates intel, writes battlecards and runs win-loss interviews, with the output delivered into the CRM. It is sold through a demo and an annual contract, and buyers report paying around $30,000 a year. Most early-stage and small teams do not need that yet. They need to hear when a competitor changes pricing, ships a feature or starts hiring in a new market, without someone checking websites by hand. That is the part WebMonitor covers.

features.title: The changes, without the program
features.body: Add competitors and WebMonitor finds their pricing, changelog, blog and careers pages, checks them on a schedule and tells you what changed. No analyst needed to keep it running.

features.title: A weekly brief your team reads
features.body: Every Monday each watchlist gets a short written summary of the week across all competitors in it, by email and in Slack.

features.title: Alerts on the changes that matter today
features.body: Add a plain-English rule to any page, such as "tell me if their Business plan price changes", and get an email as soon as it happens.

features.title: Monthly billing
features.body: Plans are $29, $79 or $149 a month and can be cancelled any time. When you outgrow it and hire a CI lead, you have a record of every competitor change to hand over.

page.limitsTitle: When Klue is the better choice
page.limits: Choose Klue if you have a CI or enablement team that will curate intel, need battlecards inside Salesforce and your sales tools, want win-loss interviews and analysis, or need intel from sources beyond public websites, such as calls, CRM notes and field reports. WebMonitor does not write battlecards, run win-loss programs or integrate with a CRM.

steps.title: Run a free snapshot
steps.body: Pick the competitor you lose the most deals to and see what WebMonitor reads on their site.

steps.title: Add the rest of your market
steps.body: Put three to ten competitors in one watchlist so the weekly brief compares them.

steps.title: Point it at your team channel
steps.body: Add a Slack webhook so the brief lands where sales and product already talk.

faq.a: Klue does not publish prices. Buyer data from Vendr puts most contracts between about $16,000 and $60,000 a year, with a median around $30,000. WebMonitor costs $348 to $1,788 a year on monthly billing.

No. WebMonitor tells you what changed on competitor websites and summarises it each week. Many small teams paste the brief into their own battlecard doc, but there is no battlecard editor or CRM integration.

For a team that mostly uses a CI tool to find out what competitors changed, yes. For a team that relies on battlecards in the CRM, win-loss analysis and curated intel from sales, no; Klue does much more.
There is a free competitor snapshot instead of a trial. Paid plans are monthly, so you can cancel after the first month if it is not useful.

snapshotCta.title: Start with a free competitor snapshot
snapshotCta.body: Enter a competitor's website and get a one-page report on their positioning, pricing, recent moves and hiring. No demo call needed.
